newsitem.title: JAPAN: World Bank to issue stg bonds for Japan investors.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to issue stg bonds for Japan investors.

text.p: The World Bank will issue about 350 million pounds worth of sterling-denominated zero coupon bonds targeted at Japanese individual investors, a bank official in Tokyo said on Thursday.

This is the first time for the World Bank to issue this type of bond. Daiwa Europe, a subsidiary of Daiwa Securities Co Ltd, will act as lead-manager for the bond which has a maturity of three years and seven months.
The payment date is December 16 and Daiwa will start selling the bond on December 13, he added.
Zero coupon bonds are sold at a discount to their face value and redeemed at par.
The difference between the discount and redemption price is commensurate with the interest on the bond.
Daiwa will set the sales price for the bond on a daily basis in line with the sterling/yen exchange rate. Sterling was at around 185.50 yen on Thursday morning in Tokyo.
The World Bank official said the idea of a sterling denominated zero coupon bond issue was proposed by Daiwa Securities.
"A majority of our fund demand is in dollars. But we don't care much about which currency the bonds will be denominated in if the issuing costs after swap live up to our target," he added.
